A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Proactive Agent and ProactiveBench work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A-D support comparison. The appendix content is unchanged apart from headers and pagination.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original reward-model assessments, proactive-agent benchmark results, inference-setting experiments and case studies.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical evaluations and additionally reports results combining multiple candidate predictions with reward-model feedback.

M1.justification: The environment gym, proactive agent, user agent, reward-model training and fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. The added joint evaluation combines two inference options already described separately in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use coding, writing and daily-life scenarios, with 6,790 agent-training events and 233 test events. The reward-model subset newly displayed in Table 1 already appears in v1's experiments; it does not add coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2 and 3. Table 4 retains GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini and LLaMA-3.1-8B while expanding their evaluated settings.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds the joint pred@3, w/ RM evaluation condition. Existing splits, training budgets, metrics, prompts and testing temperature remain unchanged. No protocol revision is reported to explain the updated main LLaMA scores.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a combined multiple-candidate and reward-feedback analysis for three models, extending v1's separate tests of those options. The existing individual analyses and failure case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting and annotator-agreement information. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Under the same reported settings, Table 3 replaces LLaMA-3.1-8B's F1 of 44.78% with 55.06% and its fine-tuned counterpart's 61.74% with 66.25%, moving the latter above GPT-4o's unchanged 64.60%. Other metrics also change. Table 4 adds combined-setting F1 scores of 79.05%, 77.53% and 74.76% for GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o and LLaMA respectively. Its revised LLaMA baseline also reverses the RM-only F1 comparison.

T1.justification: Section 3.1's task and acceptance definitions, optimization objective and Appendix C.5's metric definitions remain unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: proactive task initiation, the data-generation framework, ProactiveBench and effective fine-tuning. The headline Qwen2 result remains 66.47%; updated LLaMA numbers do not redefine the contribution claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of premature assistance, missed needs and feedback-induced silence are retained, as are limitations concerning coverage, false alarms, user evaluation and privacy. The added combined-setting sentence summarizes a new result without introducing a substantive mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, training times, processing descriptions, prompt templates, data examples and code/data access information are unchanged. Table 1 redisplays reward-model split information already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused discussion of Ask-before-plan and proactive dialogue systems, distinguishing their proactivity from task anticipation and initiation. Six references are added, including Compeer, while ChatDev and Tell Me More disappear from the bibliography. The underlying positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the related-work discussion and Section 4.3, renamed from Ablation Study to Performance Analysis. Captions and setting terminology are revised, while most prose and the overall section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reorganized around agent and reward-model subsets. Table 4 gains combined-setting rows, reordered model groups and clearer setting labels. Existing figures are retained, with Figures 2 and 4 repositioned relative to surrounding text.

improvement.justification: The joint-setting analysis and more focused related work add useful evidence and context. However, v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.2 retains LLaMA's old 44.78%-to-61.74% comparison despite Table 3's revised values, and Section 4.3 still claims RM-only improvement although 54.81% is below the revised 55.06% baseline. Two unresolved citations also appear in Section 2. These gains and regressions prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
